slot.brief: Match artificial sweeteners (aspartame, saccharin, sucralose) with their use or structure class

stem: Which artificial sweetener is a dipeptide and is unsafe for patients with phenylketonuria?
notes: from question bank g119bdcd5b979 (verified in job 20261127-115414-780e)
working:
Aspartame is the methyl ester of the dipeptide formed from aspartic acid and phenylalanine. Phenylketonuria patients cannot metabolise phenylalanine, so aspartame is unsafe for them.

Independent check: Aspartame is the methyl ester of the dipeptide aspartyl-phenylalanine. It contains phenylalanine, so it is unsuitable for patients with phenylketonuria.
solution: Aspartame is the methyl ester of the dipeptide aspartyl-phenylalanine. It contains phenylalanine, which patients with phenylketonuria cannot metabolise; hence it is unsafe for them.
